subject: Order form: invoice entity mapping, min-commit timing & tax withholding
messages:
From: Jenna Morales <jenna.morales@altiushealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@altiushealth.com, Carlos Vega <c.vega@altiushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Oct 2027 15:23:00 -0400
Subject: Order form commercial questions — invoice entity & tax withholding

Hi Karthik / Kimberly,

Thanks for sending the order form draft. A few finance questions we need clarified before Procurement can issue a PO:

1) Invoice entity mapping — our legal team requires invoices to be routed to Altius Health, Inc. (US tax ID) for US payments, but some lines of the contract will be consumed by an EU subsidiary. Can Redwood split the invoices (US entity + EU entity) or do you require a single-entity invoice? If split, how will minimum commits and proration work across entities?

2) Minimum commit timing — we plan to phase commit in two tranches (Q1 / Q3). Will Redwood accept a staged invoice cadence tied to commit tranches, or does the Order Form require upfront invoicing for the full minimum commit?

3) Tax withholding & residency evidence — our AP team requires proof of tax residency for Redwood entity to determine withholding. Please confirm what tax certificates you can provide (W-8 / VAT registration) and whether Redwood will accept the tax form before invoice issuance.

4) Net terms — Procurement needs net-45. Are you able to offer net-45 for this size of deal (DL-74219) or is net-30 the only option?

Attached a placeholder PO template for your finance folks to review. Can we get a short matrix that spells out: invoice entity options, effects on min-commit invoicing, and timing? Procurement would like to resolve by COB Wednesday so we can route the PO.

Thanks,

Jenna Morales
Head of Procurement, Altius Health
jenna.morales@altiushealth.com
Attachment: Altius_PO_Template.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Morales <jenna.morales@altiushealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Oct 2027 17:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Order form commercial questions — invoice entity & tax withholding

Hi Jenna — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up-front, then I’ll outline options and next steps.

- Invoice entity: We can invoice a single entity or split invoicing across two legal entities, but there are operational constraints (accounting complexity and potential MRR/proration impacts).
- Min-commit timing: Redwood supports staged invoicing tied to commit tranches if agreed in the Order Form; we usually do proration for partial period consumption.
- Tax residency: We can provide a W-8 BEN-E for the Redwood U.S. entity and VAT registration details for our EU entity.
- Net terms: Sales can approve net-45 for this deal size; will confirm with Finance and include in the Order Form.

Options (summary table inlined):
1) Single-entity invoice (Altius Health, Inc.)
   - All charges invoiced to US entity.
   - Redwood will handle internal allocation but taxes/residency proof accepted as standard.
   - Min-commit invoiced upfront unless customer elects staged invoice with explicit schedule.

2) Split invoicing (US + EU entity)
   - Line items mapped to consuming legal entity; separate invoices issued.
   - Minimum commit is apportioned across entities by consumption percentage; proration rules apply per tranche.
   - Requires PO(s) from both entities and additional tax evidence for each invoice.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben (Sales Ops) to confirm mechanism for staged invoices and credit/holdback treatment.
- Kimberly (Contracts) to prepare a redline that captures the chosen invoice path and net-45.
- We share a short template (Tax_Evidence_Template.xlsx) for your AP to complete so tax withholding can be evaluated ahead of invoice.

I’ve attached the current Order Form (Redwood_OrderForm_v3.pdf) for reference and a one-page matrix in the attachment. If that direction works we can set a 30-min call tomorrow to finalize.

Best,

Karthik Iyer
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_OrderForm_v3.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jenna Morales <jenna.morales@altiushealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Oct 2027 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Order form commercial questions — invoice entity & tax withholding

Adding details from Sales Ops on the staged invoicing / credit holdback side.

TL;DR: We can support staged invoicing tied to tranches with the following rules:
- Minimum commit invoiced pro-rata by tranche. Example: $600k min commit split 50/50 -> invoice $300k at tranche 1, $300k at tranche 2.
- Consumption overages billed monthly to the invoiced legal entity; overages won't be split retroactively.
- Credit/holdback: If Altius requests a holdback (e.g., 10% until go-live), we can include a holdback line item on the invoice and release it upon activation milestones.
- Accounting requirements: For split invoices, we need a PO per invoicing entity + tax evidence per entity; otherwise, all invoices must route to the single contracting entity.

Attached is a minimal template for tax residency evidence and a sample invoice cadence table.

Action items for Altius:
- Confirm whether you will provide a US PO only, or POs from both US and EU entities.
- Confirm net-45 request so we can get Finance approval (Karthik will coordinate).

Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
Attachment: Tax_Evidence_Template.xlsx

From: Carlos Vega <c.vega@altiushealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jenna Morales <jenna.morales@altiushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Oct 2027 11:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Order form commercial questions — invoice entity & tax withholding

Thanks, team. A couple clarifying points from Procurement / AP: 

- We can provide a PO for the US entity this week. Getting a PO from the EU subsidiary will take longer (legal approvals). Would Redwood accept a temporary single-entity invoice while EU invoicing is sorted, with a follow-up intercompany allocation?
- Net-45 is required for our procurement policy. If Redwood can get Finance sign off, we will proceed.
- On holdback: acceptable if documented in the Order Form; need the milestone definition (what constitutes "activation").

If you can confirm the single-entity temporary path and provide the activation milestone language for the holdback, Procurement will sign the PO and route it to AP.

Carlos Vega
Senior Procurement Manager, Altius Health
c.vega@altiushealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@altiushealth.com>, Jenna Morales <jenna.morales@altiushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Order form commercial questions — invoice entity & tax withholding

Carlos / Jenna — good plan. Confirming final position and next steps below so we have a paper trail for Procurement / AP: 

1) Temporary single-entity invoice path: Yes — Redwood will accept Altius Health, Inc. (US) as the invoiced party initially. We will support an intercompany allocation after the EU entity is able to issue a PO, but intercompany re-billing is a customer-side operational step (we will provide the consumption report to support it).

2) Minimum commit & staged invoicing: We will prorate the minimum commit by tranche per the Sales Ops approach (example in Ben's attachment). Order Form will include a table: tranche dates, tranche invoice amounts, and proration rules for mid-tranche activation.

3) Holdback / activation milestone language (suggested):
   - "A holdback equal to 10% of the tranche invoice shall be held by Customer and released upon completion of the Activation Milestone, defined as: (a) successful integration test demonstrating end-to-end inference at 90% of agreed throughput for 3 consecutive business days; and (b) Customer confirmation of production readiness."

4) Net terms: Redwood will accept net-45 for DL-74219 pending final Finance confirmation. I will follow up with a one-line Finance approval note before signature.

5) TAX EVIDENCE: Please complete the attached Tax_Evidence_Template.xlsx and return to finance@redwood.com. We will not require the tax evidence to sign the PO, but AP will need it prior to issuing the first invoice if the split invoicing route is chosen.

6) Next steps: Kimberly will issue a redline to the Order Form that captures the chosen invoice path, holdback language, and net-45. I’m attaching a draft redline now for your legal team to review. If that looks good, we’ll route to DocuSign for signature.

Link to DocuSign pre-fill: https://www.docusign.com/ALTIUS-RW-74219-sign

Thanks — I’ll ping Finance for final net-45 approval and loop back.

Best,

Karthik Iyer
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Attachment: OrderForm_Redline_MSA_20271010.docx
